text:
maya: heads up — saw repeated latency spikes during a tenant warmup test this morning. sequence looks like: prefetch kicks in -> prefix cache fills -> eviction kicks out a different tenant's hot prefix -> that tenant's lease gets transferred -> that causes a cascade of re-prefetches and 200-300ms p95 blips. anyone seen this pattern?

samir: yep, saw something similar in canary last week. can you paste the eviction logs / metric slices? curious about eviction score deltas and whether the prefill is using hard eviction credits or soft reservations.

maya: here are the relevant snippets (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-21T09:17:03Z] prefetch: tenant=acme prefix=/usr/42 size=1.2MB
[2026-03-21T09:17:03Z] eviction: victim=tenant=pegasus prefix=/auth token=0xabc score=92 -> evict
[2026-03-21T09:17:03Z] lease: transfer start from node-a -> node-c (grace=0)
[2026-03-21T09:17:03Z] prefetch: tenant=pegasus missing -> re-prefetch scheduled
```

maya: we don't have a way to say "prefill but don't steal hard credits" today. prefill behaves identical to demand loads from the eviction scoring POV.

lee: two quick ideas: 1) a quiet-warmup window where prefetch inserts with a lower base score (effectively a soft pin) for X seconds, letting them coexist unless memory pressure gets extreme; 2) ephemeral reservation tokens that live only while the prefetch task is active (not counted against tenant eviction credits). tradeoffs: fairness vs cold-start latency.

lee: metrics we should add: per-prefetch evict-causes (count how often prefetch causes eviction), time-between-prefetch-and-evict, and a histogram of eviction-score-deltas when prefetch runs. without that we're guessing.

dave: related — in the handoff postmortem we had a similar oscillation when lease transfers had zero grace and immediate demote. PR #2743 added a small demote grace but that only helped steady-state. Warmup is different because it simultaneously raises memory pressure across prefixes. I prototyped ephemeral reservations in a spike (branch: spikes/prefetch-reservations). sketch:
```
// prefetch reservation pseudocode
reserve = prefetch_reserve(size)
if (!reserve) {
  // fallback to low-priority prefill (no reservation)
  prefill_with_low_score(prefix)
} else {
  prefill_with_reservation(prefix)
  release_reservation_on_complete(prefix)
}
```

dave: downside: if the node crashes while reservation held we need sequencer reconciliation or TTL-based expiry. but simpler than changing eviction scoring globally.

maya: crash case is my big concern — if we hold ephemeral reservations and the node dies, other nodes might assume capacity is used and start evicting, or worse, two nodes think they've reserved the same space. how do we make this safe?

samir: keep reservations local and soft — they only prevent prefetch-driven eviction, not demand-driven eviction. second line: attach a short TTL (e.g., 10s) and have sequencer reconcile at lease movements. if node crashes, TTL expires and things fall back to normal. also add a reconciliation hook that clears reservations on successful lease transfer.

lee: implementation notes: - add prefetch tag on prefixes in cache metadata (boolean + expiry) - eviction scorer subtracts a configurable delta when tag present - expirer task sweeps stale tags. Should be backwards compatible and feature-flagged.

maya: sounds reasonable. any correctness holes re: read-after-write or strong invariants?

samir: correctness: as long as prefetch reservations never block demand reads (reads always win), we won't introduce correctness bugs. The main risk is fairness — a malicious heavy prefetcher could hold many soft reservations. we MUST cap total reservation bytes per-node and per-tenant and surface metrics.

perf-bot: experiment queued: spikes/prefetch-reservations -> stack=staging, duration=48h. CI: unit tests + small chaos run. :thumbsup:

maya: action items: 1) samir to prototype reservation TTL + sequencer reconcile spike (branch mentioned) 2) lee to add the three metrics above + dashboard 3) dave to draft a short RFC with tradeoffs (memory overhead, fairness caps, crash TTL) — target end of week for spike results.

maya: thanks all, will follow up with logs after the staging run. :coffee:
